skill.name: inference-sh
skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps for images, video, LLM calls, search, audio, 3D, and Twitter automation.
skill.summary: Run cloud AI apps through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: Confirmed critical remote-installer findings where curl output is piped directly into sh. Most API key, shell completion, documentation URL, and Markdown backtick matches are false positives. Semantic review found broad infsh CLI permission and Twitter/X automation risks that need guardrails before publication.

remediation.issue: Remote install script piped to shell
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell installation with signed packages, checksum verification, or manual download steps. Pin versions and document verification before execution.
Restrict allowed commands to required read-only discovery and explicit app run workflows. Require confirmation for deploy, pull, update, and file-write commands.

remediation.issue: Social media automation lacks explicit guardrails
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before posting, sending DMs, following, liking, or retweeting. Show the final text and target account before execution.
Advise users to store INFSH_API_KEY in a secret manager and avoid pasting production secrets into prompts or saved input files.

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Permission Scope
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash(infsh *), which permits any inference.sh CLI subcommand. The CLI reference includes deployment and source pull commands, so agent actions can exceed simple app runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools line is explicit, and the CLI reference documents deploy and pull subcommands. The risk depends on agent behavior, but permission scope is broad.

semantic_findings.title: Social Media Automation Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill examples include posting to Twitter/X and list DM, follow, like, and retweet actions. These actions can create account activity without careful confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly show social media posting and account interaction capabilities. The finding is about user-account impact, not command syntax.

content.value_statement: AI model workflows often require separate APIs, credentials, and task tracking. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use inference.sh CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides inference.sh CLI setup, login, update, and authentication checks.
Discovers apps by category, search term, featured status, newest listing, or page.
Runs cloud apps with inline input or saved input files.
Generates sample input files and inspects app schemas before execution.
Tracks long-running tasks and retrieves or saves results.
References image, video, LLM, search, audio, 3D, and Twitter app examples.
limitations: Requires the external inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account.
Runs cloud services that may use credits or provider-specific limits.
Does not verify remote install scripts, package signatures, or model outputs.
Some workflows can create public or private social media actions.

use_cases.title: Generate Media Assets
use_cases.description: Create image, video, audio, or 3D outputs from cloud AI apps without managing local GPUs.

use_cases.title: Prototype Model Workflows
use_cases.description: Find models, inspect schemas, create sample inputs, and run tasks from one CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Run Research Tasks
use_cases.description: Use search and LLM apps to gather information, summarize findings, and track long-running jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Find Apps by Category
prompt_templates.prompt: Use inference.sh to list image generation apps. Show the best options and explain what each app is for.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Sample Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe sample input for a FLUX image app, explain each field, and ask before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Track a Long Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a video generation task without waiting, capture the task ID, and check status until the result is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-App Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow that searches for references, generates a script, creates a video, and saves final outputs for review.

output_examples.input: Find a fast image model for a product concept render.
output_examples.output: The skill would list relevant image apps, compare speed and quality, then recommend a model to run.

output_examples.input: Run a long video task and tell me when it is done.
output_examples.output: The skill would submit the task, record the task ID, check progress, and summarize the final result link.

output_examples.input: Prepare a social post but do not publish it yet.
output_examples.output: The skill would draft the post text and ask for explicit approval before any Twitter/X action.

best_practices: Review every command before execution, especially install, deploy, and social media commands.
Use scoped API keys and store them in a secret manager.
Pin app versions when reproducibility matters.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers into a shell without verification.
Do not post, like, follow, or send messages without explicit approval.
Do not paste production secrets into prompt text or saved input files.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant use the inference.sh CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI needs authentication before it can run most app workflows.

faq.question: Can it run image and video models?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents image, video, audio, LLM, search, 3D, and utility app categories.

faq.question: Can it call Claude models?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include Claude through OpenRouter and other LLM app routes.

faq.question: Does it perform network calls?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI connects to inference.sh cloud services and may return hosted result URLs.

faq.question: Is Twitter automation safe to use?
faq.answer: Use it carefully. Always review the final text and target account before posting or sending messages.
